_comment_purpose: Vocab overlay for --mode report (llm_cognition variant). Merged on top of templates/agents/llm_cognition/vocab.json by setup.sh; only fields whose meaning changes under report mode appear here. Fields not listed inherit from the base llm_cognition vocab.
_comment_scope: Report mode redeploys only the referee* trio plus the audit agents — none of the generative agents run. We override only what the referee* bodies (which DO run, with shared_modes/report/ body overlays) actually need rewritten.
_comment_referee_journal_role: The base referee-core.md treats the paper as if produced by this pipeline (its own draft). Under report mode the paper is an external submission under review; we re-anchor the venue-role string so the referee internalizes that framing.
REFEREE_JOURNAL_ROLE: **top ML venue** (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR) or TMLR, evaluating an external submission under review
_comment_mech_eval_frame: The report-mode referee-mechanism overlay body keys its evaluative frame; report mode names the math-auditor explicitly (the base value says 'another referee'), so the frame is re-anchored here per variant.
MECH_EVAL_FRAME: **You evaluate whether the paper's computational mechanism works as a real account of the behavior** — not whether the math is correct (the math-auditor handles that), not whether the paper fits the venue (the editorial referee handles that). Your question is: does the computational force the paper invokes actually deliver the result the paper claims, through the channel the paper claims, for reasons a skeptical ML audience would find convincing?
_comment_verdict_note: The base llm_cognition REFEREE_VERDICT_NOTE routes through the pipeline's editor agent and tier table, neither of which exists in a report deployment (report-synthesizer aggregates; no stage docs are installed). This override keeps the conference-cadence translation and re-anchors the routing sentence.
REFEREE_VERDICT_NOTE: > **Verdict semantics for this variant.** The recommendation set below is standard journal-cadence vocabulary; the conference venues this submission targets have no Minor Revision, Major Revision, or Revise-and-Resubmit — the real outcome space is accept/reject with one rebuttal round. Read **Minor Revision** as "a rebuttal or camera-ready cycle absorbs these changes," **Major Revision** as "reject this cycle; the listed changes are what a resubmission next cycle must fix," and **Revise and Resubmit** the same way with larger scope. Use the standard tokens so the report-synthesizer can aggregate mechanically; where the conference-cadence reading changes what the authors should actually do, say so in your report prose.
